topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation, cancer genetics, and genetic instability.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the historical discovery of viral and cellular oncogenes and the experimental assays used to detect cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and mutational mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions, cell cycle regulatory pathways, and dosage effects distinguishing oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how DNA repair defects and mitotic errors generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how the progressive accumulation of mutations and inherited genetic defects drive tumor development and adaptation.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by offering reading recommendations and previewing the next session.
